name: Hot Water Reflex Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical criteria for Hot Water Reflex Epilepsy

criteria.description: Seizures consistently triggered by hot water exposure, typically during bathing
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing ictal epileptiform discharges during or immediately after hot water exposure
Exclusion of other epilepsy syndromes or neurological disorders that could explain seizures
Detailed clinical history confirming reproducible seizure episodes with hot water stimulus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of seizures triggered by hot water exposure with supportive EEG findings and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by EEG; video-EEG monitoring during hot water exposure may be required.

pathognomonic.notes: Seizures occur immediately or shortly after hot water exposure
searchTerms: seizures triggered by hot water causing full body convulsions
generalized seizures from hot water exposure

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hot water-induced focal seizures with impaired awareness
searchTerms: partial seizures with impaired awareness from hot water
focal seizures triggered by hot water
warning signs before hot water seizures
aura before seizure triggered by hot water

common.symptomName: Myoclonic jerks triggered by hot water
searchTerms: sudden jerks caused by hot water
myoclonic movements triggered by hot water
involuntary muscle jerks from hot water

common.symptomName: Autonomic symptoms during seizures (e.g., sweating, palpitations)
searchTerms: sweating and fast heartbeat during seizures
light sensitivity during or after seizures
eye discomfort from seizure light sensitivity
unable to speak during focal seizures

rare.symptomName: Status epilepticus triggered by hot water exposure
searchTerms: prolonged seizures triggered by hot water
status epilepticus from hot water exposure
continuous seizures after hot water contact

laboratory: Serum electrolytes to exclude metabolic causes
imaging: Brain MRI typically normal or may show nonspecific changes
Video-EEG monitoring demonstrating ictal discharges triggered by hot water
other: Provocation testing with hot water under controlled conditions may reproduce seizures

distinguishingFeatures: Seizures triggered by fever rather than hot water
Typically occur in children under 5 years
Seizures triggered by flashing lights or visual stimuli
No association with hot water exposure
Seizures triggered by stimuli other than hot water (e.g., reading, music)

redFlags: Seizures occurring without hot water exposure
references: Singh S, et al. Hot water epilepsy: clinical and EEG features. Epilepsia. 2019.
Bhatia MS, et al. Reflex epilepsies: a clinical review. Neurol India. 2020.
